data.description:
The company

It's still difficult for business owners to sell their business, or buy others, in the sub-£10m enterprise value market. Information asymmetry, lack of knowledge and low transaction values make it hard, and most M&A firms shy away from the segment because they can't serve it profitably. A generation of owner-managers is approaching retirement, and most of them have no realistic route to a sale.

manda exists to fix that. We match buyers with sellers in the part of the market everyone else ignores, and we finance acquisitions ourselves so buyers arrive pre-qualified and often pre-financed. We've sold the first businesses, funded the first acquisition loans, and we're now opening the platform up beyond the businesses that already bank with us.

manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders. Since 2012 iwoca has provided more than £4 billion in funding and its mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments. That backing is why we can serve this market where others can't: a deep footprint in the SME economy with 150,000+ UK customers, the data and infrastructure of an established lender, and the ability to build clean, automated processes instead of running an advisory firm on spreadsheets.

We’re looking for a Partnership Manager - manda (iwoca's M&A Platform)

We're looking for someone to build the introducer network that brings business owners to manda, iwoca's M&A platform. Accountants, solicitors, wealth managers and brokers meet an owner who is thinking about retiring long before we do. Your job is to make sure that when they do they think of us, and that referring us is the easiest thing they do that day.

The role

Your mission is to build a referral channel that produces a steady flow of business owners who are genuinely ready to sell.

Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but the pool is finite. The professionals who already advise business owners are the most credible route to the ones we'd otherwise never reach, and right now we have no systematic way of working with them.

You'll be starting from close to nothing, so the first version of this channel is yours to design. It also means the job is as much about making referrals actually arrive as it is about signing partners up.

It also has to scale. In this industry most partner flow still depends on people turning up at industry events, which works but stops the moment you stop showing up. We're after the version of this channel where referring a client to manda takes a couple of clicks inside the software an adviser already uses.

Key responsibilities include:

Build the introducer network

  • Find and win the firms worth working with: accountancy practices, corporate finance boutiques, solicitors, wealth managers and business transfer agents. Work out which kinds of firm actually refer, and concentrate there.

  • Do the outbound yourself. Identify the firm, get the meeting, make the case, and follow up until something happens.

  • Design what we offer them: how a referral is made, what the partner gets, what we commit to in return, and how we keep them informed once their client is with us.

Make referrals actually arrive

  • A signed partnership is worth nothing until a referral comes through. You'll own the ongoing relationship work that turns agreements into a flow: regular contact, keeping manda front of mind, briefing partner teams, and being the person they call.

  • Track referral volume and quality by partner, and be honest about which relationships aren't working so we can stop spending time on them.

Make the channel scale

  • Judge every partnership by whether it adds referrals without adding work. A relationship that only produces when you're in the room isn't a channel yet.

  • Work out which partner technology is worth plugging into: the practice management and accounting software advisers already work in, tracked referral links and partner portals, and integrations that let a firm refer a client without leaving their own tools. You won't build these yourself, but you'll identify them, make the commercial case, and scope them with our Product Builder.

  • Look for partners who can bring a book rather than one client at a time. One firm with hundreds of owner-managed clients is worth more to us than ten firms with five, if we can find a way to surface the right candidates across the whole book.

Work iwoca's existing network

  • iwoca already has a broker network and a partnerships function with relationships across the SME economy. Working out where manda fits into those relationships is far faster than starting cold, and it's the first place to look.

Events and community

  • Build a focused programme of events worth attending and, where it makes sense, running our own: succession and exit planning, accountancy and adviser events, industry gatherings, and business owner peer communities.

  • Judge them on referrals rather than attendance, and stop going to the ones that don't produce. Events are how you find and land partners, not how the channel scales.

Prove the channel pays

  • Establish what a referral actually costs us once your time, any partner incentives and events are counted, and how many convert into a signed mandate. We have an assumption in our financial model and nobody has yet tested it.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Essential:

  • Around 4+ years in partnerships, channel or business development, ideally B2B, where you built or substantially grew a referral channel rather than inheriting one that already worked.

  • You've done the full cycle yourself: identified the target firms, got the meetings, agreed the terms, and then managed the relationship afterwards.

  • A background in M&A, marketplaces, business broking or business transfer.

  • You understand that the work starts after the agreement is signed, and you have the discipline to keep a channel warm over months rather than weeks.

  • Numerate and honest about performance. You track referrals by partner, you know which relationships are producing, and you say so when one isn't.

  • You think in systems as well as relationships. You can tell the difference between a partnership that scales and one that only works while you're pushing it, and you'd rather replace your own manual work with an integration than defend it.

  • Comfortable specifying technology without building it. You can look at a partner's tools and our product, work out what would make us the path of least resistance, and scope it clearly enough for a product team to build.

  • Genuinely hands-on. There's no team to delegate to: you'll build the target list, send the emails, run the meetings and keep the CRM straight yourself.

  • A commercial thinker with a bias for action, comfortable navigating ambiguity in an early-stage venture.

Bonus:

  • Experience with accountancy, legal or wealth management channels specifically.

  • Experience running an event programme with commercial targets attached to it.

  • Familiarity with the UK succession and exit planning landscape.

  • Comfortable treating a CRM as a discipline rather than an afterthought, ideally HubSpot.

  • You've shipped a partner integration, an embedded referral flow or a software marketplace listing, or worked closely with a product team on one.

  • Familiar with the software UK accountancy practices and advisers actually work in, such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, IRIS or Dext.

The salary

We expect to pay £55,000–£80,000 and an annual performance based bonus for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

The Role

We are looking for a seasoned IT Engineer II to join our Engineering team. At this level, you have developed your skill set to confidently tackle all but the most complex problems affecting the team. You will lead the delivery of essential IT services and small to medium-sized projects, either independently or by guiding other engineers.

 

As an Engineer II, you are an individual contributor with a deep understanding of your team’s purpose and how it impacts Checkout as a whole. You will act as an owner-operator, taking accountability for the success of the systems within your area of responsibility.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Project Leadership: Independently design and deliver project-level work with minimal guidance from senior engineers.

  • Atlassian Mastery: Act as a subject matter expert for our Workplace Technology stack, with a specific focus on high-level administration and optimisation of Jira and Confluence.

  • Operational Excellence: Provide an advanced level of operational support on team-owned services and train new members on service design, security, and operations.

  • Incident Response: Display urgency and accountability during incidents, triaging and supporting complex flows unaided.

  • Mentorship: Regularly support and mentor less experienced engineers, helping to raise the technical quality of the team.

  • Automation: Proactively recognise areas for improvement and suggest automated solutions (Python/PowerShell) to reduce incidental complexity.

 

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience: Typically 2–3+ years of experience in an IT Engineering or similar technical role.

  • Technical Expertise: Experience with Identity Providers (Okta, Azure AD) and protocols like SAML and SCIM.

  • Advanced Atlassian Skills: High-level experience managing the Atlassian suite. You should be comfortable with complex Jira configurations, workflow customisations, and permission schemes.

  • Problem Solving: A logical approach to troubleshooting, with the ability to articulate technical trade-offs between different solutions.

  • Ownership: A proactive "owner-operator" mindset—you take responsibility for your tasks and the long-term health of the systems you manage.

  • Communication: Ability to communicate effectively with company stakeholders and resolve complex support queries within your area of focus.

Adaptability: Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where you can balance temporary workarounds with flexible, long-term architectural solutions.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

About Userlane

Userlane is a software adoption platform that shows enterprises whether their software and AI investments are actually working. Our team works with some of the biggest names in regulated industries, helping them get real value from technology and giving their employees the right support inside software applications they use every day. Based in Munich, growing internationally.

Userlane combines Application Intelligence and Contextual Assistance for regulated industries. Application Intelligence shows where software creates cost and friction across the estate. Contextual Assistance helps people get work done in the moment, without training burden. We work with healthcare organizations across the US and Europe, helping clinical and operational teams work confidently in complex systems like EHRs and other core clinical and business applications.


Your mission

Own Application Intelligence at Userlane. You'll shape what we build across App Discovery, HEART Analytics and Portfolio Overview to help enterprise CIOs and IT leaders see where software spending delivers value and where it creates waste. You'll work on opportunities such as:

  • Defining metrics that hold up: Own the methodology behind our HEART Analytics, deciding what each score measures, how it's calculated, and how it stays credible when data is incomplete.

  • Delivering outcome-linked metrics: Connect usage data to business outcomes like cost savings, efficiency and compliance risk that enterprise executives can take action on

  • Building for time-poor executives: Design analytics that bring insights to leaders and answers "what should I do?" not just "what happened?"

  • Connecting fragmented data sources: Define the integration strategy to combine Userlane behavioural data with cost data from SAM tools, license data from IT asset management and employee data from HR systems,

  • Transforming insights into action: Define what turns raw usage data into insights that drive action, not just dashboards people look at once

  • AI adoption governance: Extend analytics to measure how AI assistants and agents affect productivity, cost and ROI.


Your profile

  • 5+ years of product management experience on data/analytics products within a modern product organisation

  • You've defined a metrics methodology, scoring system or measurement framework that others build on, and you can defend the trade-offs behind it. You're comfortable reasoning about why one calculation approach produces misleading results in a specific scenario and another doesn't.

  • You start with the business question, not the data. Your first instinct is "what decision are they trying to make?" rather than "what data do we have?"

  • You hold your ground. You'll work with technically strong colleagues and leaders with well-formed opinions. You can disagree with them credibly, engage with their reasoning, and change your position when the evidence says so, not when the seniority does.

  • You can hold a credible conversation with data engineers and data scientists about what the data can and cannot prove, and you understand the difference between interesting data and actionable insight

  • You've worked in enterprise B2B (not B2C product analytics). Healthcare experience is a strong plus

  • You figure out what works by talking to customers and watching them use the product

  • You're capable of explaining things to engineers, salespeople, support agents and CEOs alike

  • You're fluent in English (spoken and written)


What's in for you

  • Team & Culture: A high-performance culture with great leadership and a fun, engaged, motivated and diverse team with people from over 20 countries

  • Impact: You'll be part of an empowered cross-functional team given the freedom and autonomy to solve real customer problems

  • Product strategy influence: Work directly with our VP Product to shape our 2026-2030 strategy as we expand into new sectors

  • Market: Userlane is among the global leaders in the rapidly growing Digital Adoption industry

  • Growth: We take you and your development seriously. You can expect weekly 121s, a personalised skills assessment and development plan, on-the-job coaching and budget for events and training
    Benefits: We offer flexible benefits related to savings and security, health and well-being, and lifestyle and leisure

This role sits at the intersection of pre-sales engineering, telephony architecture, and enterprise contact center strategy. You will act as a trusted advisor to enterprise prospects and customers, guiding them through complex, ambiguous voice deployment conversations—from SIP trunking and call routing to media handling and real-time transcription—ensuring Decagon integrates seamlessly into their existing contact center platforms while meeting latency, reliability, and compliance requirements.

As an early hire in this function, you will define best practices for voice deployment solutioning, partner cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Engineering, and set the standard for how Decagon engages with enterprises running mission-critical contact center operations. You will establish technical credibility with stakeholders across the C-suite, telephony and network teams, contact center operations, and CX leadership.

In this role, you will

  • Partner with Account Executives to discover, qualify, and design voice deployment solutions that address customer telephony constraints and deliver measurable containment and CX outcomes.

  • Design SIP integration approaches—BYOC trunking, REFER-based transfer, header propagation, and media/streaming paths (Websockets, Audio Connector, External Voice Transfer)—tailored to each customer's topology and security posture.

  • Diagnose complex, multi-leg call flows down to the packet level, and establish repeatable methods for tracing and resolving SIP and media issues in production.

  • Establish scalable pre-sales processes, deployment playbooks, and reusable reference architectures to support growth.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. Kraken's Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, static and 3D design, motion design, AI video creative and web design, turning growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, holding the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

 

The opportunity

As our Senior Performance Creative, you concept, produce and ship paid creative for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Paid static is the center of the role, but we're hiring a hybrid rather than a specialist: this means you also ideate and create performance video and treat gen AI as a core production method rather than a novelty. You take a project from idea to a finished, approved, multi-market asset set, and you bring a real feel for what people stop on, share and screenshot.

 

You report to the Creative Lead, Consumer Creative & Design, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. Senior here means craft and automation leadership: you set the bar for paid static on the team, work with AI enabled processes, collaborate closely with other Krakenites in and outside the team, and are the person others come to with performance creative questions.

  • Own paid static for Kraken Consumer across product launches, campaigns, promotions and always-on activity.

  • Build for channels like Meta, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Reddit and X. You know what wins where, and you build to each platform's specs and native feel.

  • Concept and cut performance video so campaigns ship as complete cross-format sets, from 9:16 sound-on to static-adjacent 1:1 and 4:5.

  • Produce AI-generated and AI-assisted video and imagery, and know when AI is the fastest route to a great ad and when it isn't.

  • Bring ideas to briefs rather than executing them literally. Pitch culturally timely, internet-native concepts that nobody asked for, and build the winners into creative pillars we can keep using.

  • Version and localize at scale across markets, languages, formats and regulatory requirements. In a typical month you'll have roughly a dozen workstreams in flight at once, most spanning several formats and several markets.

  • Build creative that's designed to be tested. Performance Marketing owns test design, cadence and readouts. You own the creative response: reading the results, forming a point of view on why a variant won, and turning that into the next round of hooks, concepts and cuts.

  • Partner with Product Marketing, compliance and regional teams to get work approved without losing the idea.

  • Hold a high craft bar on your own work and keep your files clean enough for other people to build on.

     

What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in performance creative at a high-volume in-house team or performance agency, ideally in fintech, crypto, gaming or another regulated category.

  • A portfolio that proves it, submitted with your application. Paid static above all, with the brief or objective alongside the work and the result where you're able to share it. Include two or three full video cuts, at least one AI-generated or AI-assisted piece with a short note on what was tooling and what was you, and one concept you tested where you can talk us through what the data said and what you changed.

  • Layout, hierarchy, type and composition that hold up at thumbnail size, in feed, and in multiple languages.

  • Platform-native instincts across Meta, TikTok and YouTube. You can explain why the same idea needs a different build on each one.

  • Real video skills, from concept to finished, sound-designed cut.

  • High-level command of gen AI video and image tooling, with shipped work to show for it.

  • Experience inside a structured creative testing program. You're fluent in the metrics your creative moves (thumb-stop rate, hook rate, CTR, CVR, CPA and ROAS), you can tell a real winner from low performers, and can translate test results into a creative decision.

  • Fluency in internet and meme culture, with comedic timing and an instinct for what's about to feel dated.

  • Speed without sloppiness. Comfortable with fast turnarounds, several review rounds and late changes.

  • Comfort working inside regulatory constraints, with layouts that survive risk warnings and market-specific requirements.

  • A solid copywriting instinct. Plain language, value first, no hype and no jargon.

  • Figma and Adobe CC (After Effects, Premiere, Photoshop) as well as strong genAI skills

  • Curious about investing and crypto at a minimum, and able to make the space legible to others.

About the Role

We're looking for a Detection Engineer to own the detection content that powers the Artemis platform. You'll design, build, test, and continuously tune high-fidelity detections across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS environments — treating detection as code, and using AI as a force multiplier at every step: authoring rules with AI assistance, and building anomaly detections that learn what's normal in each environment and flag what isn't. Detections at Artemis don't just fire alerts; they feed an AI-native investigation pipeline, so precision, rich context, and machine-readable output matter as much as coverage. This is a hands-on engineering role where every rule you ship directly determines what threats we catch for customers and how fast we catch them.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain the detection library - Design, implement, and own high-fidelity detections across cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), identity (Okta, Entra ID), endpoint (EDR), and SaaS log sources, from hypothesis to production.

  • Practice detection-as-code - Manage detection content like software: version-controlled rules, peer review, automated validation and testing, and CI/CD deployment across customer environments.

  • Map and close coverage gaps - Measure detection coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, prioritize gaps based on real-world threat activity, and systematically close them.

  • Validate against real attacks - Build and run attack simulations and test harnesses to prove detections fire on true positives and stay quiet on benign activity, before and after they ship.

  • Tune relentlessly - Own false-positive and false-negative rates across the fleet: analyze detection performance data, tune noisy logic at the source, and sunset detections that no longer earn their keep.

  • Use AI to write detections at scale - Leverage AI throughout the detection lifecycle: use AI-assisted workflows to author, convert, test, and document rules faster than any traditional team could, and build the tooling that makes AI-generated detection content trustworthy enough to ship.

  • Build behavioral and anomaly-based detections - Go beyond static signatures: establish behavioral baselines of normal activity per environment (identity, cloud, SaaS usage patterns) and engineer anomaly detections that surface deviations — impossible travel, unusual privilege use, novel API activity — with high signal and low noise.

  • Engineer detections for AI-powered investigation - Design detections that produce rich, structured context so the Artemis platform can investigate and resolve cases autonomously.

  • Turn intelligence into detections - Translate threat intelligence, incident findings, and threat hunt results from our research and SOC teams into durable, behavioral detection logic.

  • Partner with the SOC and research teams - Close the loop with Apollo analysts and security researchers: use case outcomes and analyst feedback to drive detection improvements, and give them documentation that makes every alert investigable.

  • Support customer-specific tuning - Adapt and tune detection content to each customer's environment and business context, reducing noise without sacrificing coverage.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on cybersecurity experience, with significant time in detection engineering

  • Proven track record designing, building, and tuning detections at scale across SIEM, EDR, or custom detection platforms

  • Strong proficiency in detection languages and formats such as Sigma, KQL, SPL, or YARA-L, and comfort writing code (Python preferred) for automation and testing

  • Deep knowledge of attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (MITRE ATT&CK) and how they manifest in logs across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS telemetry

  • Experience with detection-as-code workflows: Git, peer review, automated testing, and CI/CD for detection content

  • Experience using AI tools to accelerate detection authoring, tuning, or validation — and judgment about when AI-generated logic is ready to ship

  • Experience building behavioral or anomaly-based detections: establishing baselines of normal activity and engineering detections that flag meaningful deviations

  • Strong log-analysis skills and demonstrated ability to distinguish malicious activity from benign noise across diverse data sources

  • Clear written and verbal communication — able to document detection logic and explain coverage and trade-offs to engineers, analysts, and customers

Bonus

  • Experience in an MDR, MSSP, or high-volume SOC environment

  • Experience with attack simulation and validation frameworks (Atomic Red Team, purple teaming)

  • Background in threat hunting or incident response across cloud environments

  • Experience with UEBA platforms or statistical/ML-based detection methods (peer grouping, time-series baselining, outlier scoring)

  • Experience building AI-assisted detection or investigation tooling from scratch

  • Contributions to open-source detection content or the broader detection engineering community

Why Work at Artemis?

  • Make a real world impact. You'll lead the human layer of defense that protects real companies. Every standard you set and process you sharpen raises the quality of protection customers depend on.

  • Be challenged to be better than ever before. Our team includes some of the smartest and most driven people in the world. We guarantee you will learn more in 1 year here than 10 years in another place.

Senior Producer

ScapeWorld Entertainment

Remote. Our working day runs on CET, wherever you sit. Full time, on a long-term contract. Starting as soon as you can. Where you live while you do is up to you; the location field on this posting only fits one country, so please read this as the real rule and apply from wherever you are.

About us

We are Scape, a Swedish game studio of about 30 people, fully remote by choice. We are launching Scape on Steam Early Access later this year: a growing platform of multiplayer games where a player's identity carries across all of them. The first game inside Scape is Gravity: a precision climbing game where 100 players share one server, one tower, and one long way down. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios, Epic and Ubisoft.

Since we are a small team about to put our first game in front of players, we are looking for the person who holds the plan, the priorities and the team together while we do it. If that sounds like you, we would love to meet.

The role

Let us start with the studio you would be joining. Around thirty people, fully remote, and a group of strong leads in design, art, engineering, QA, community and commercial who own their crafts and run their own teams. What we do not have is the person who looks across all of them at once, holds the plan they are all working to, and makes the day-to-day calls that keep it moving as one. That is this role. It is the only production seat in the company, and it comes with real authority.

You would work closely with the Creative Director. They own what the game is, set the direction and make the big bets. You own the plan that gets us there and the decisions inside it: scope, sequencing and trade-offs within a milestone are yours to make, and you decide which questions need to reach them and which do not. They should be able to step back and know that things are being handled, because they are.

In practice, it comes down to four things:

You know how a game gets made. You can see what depends on what, where the effort really sits, and whether an estimate is going to hold. When a lead tells you how long something takes, you know how to hear it and what has to land for the work to ship on time.

You own the plan and the priorities. Not just the schedule, but the order of work behind it. When two things compete, you decide, or you get the decision made and tell everyone affected. Open questions have an owner and a date. Nothing sits unanswered because nobody was sure whose call it was.

You plan ahead. Problems get found while they are still cheap, and everything that has to land together lands together: builds, assets, store material, localization, press dates.

You lead the team's delivery. People know the plan is real, feel good about hitting it, and are still standing when it ships. The leads lead their crafts. You lead how it all comes together, and you meet each team where it is: some want you in the weeds with them on estimates and sequencing, others mainly need the picture across teams kept current. You read which is which.

We have a production pipeline that works, and like any pipeline it can always be better. You would inherit it as it is, get to know it and the people who run it, and then improve it where you see the need. Nobody here expects you to arrive with all the answers. We do hope you arrive curious about how we work and comfortable telling us, kindly and clearly, where we could do better.


What you will own

  • Production priorities day to day: the order of work across the studio, the trade-off calls within a milestone, and every open question that is blocking someone. You find who can answer, get it answered or escalated with a clear recommendation attached, and close the loop with the teams waiting on it. If a question is blocking someone, it is yours until it is not

  • Keeping design, art, engineering, QA and marketing in step with each other, week by week, so nobody is working against a version of the plan that has moved

  • The forward view: every feature in flight, what each one is still waiting on, the handoffs between departments caught early, and risk seen while it is still cheap, named, and carrying a mitigation before it turns into a schedule event

  • The team's delivery health: sustainable pace, morale, and delivery on target, treated as one problem rather than a trade-off

  • Marketing as a real production dependency, and the alignment dates around release: builds, assets, store material, localization drops, press dates, landing on time and together

  • The production plan behind all of it: a milestone schedule with a baseline, a forecast per milestone from velocity against remaining scope, estimates held against actuals, and replanning on a cycle rather than after something breaks

  • QA in step with everyone else. Our QA lead owns testing; you make sure QA knows what is coming and when, that testable builds land when the plan says they do, and that the QA window sits in the schedule where it belongs rather than where it ends up

  • External production partners: localization, video, 3D, anything we outsource. You own the relationship and the communication in both directions, and you chase. Briefs and context going out, deliveries coming in and landing in the build, and the schedule that keeps them in step with everyone else. Leads should never have to chase a partner themselves. The craft stays with the partner; making it fit is on you

  • The production process itself and the tools it runs through. We use Jira, including Jira Plans for planning months out against a baseline, and you own it for the studio. You also support hiring managers through their recruitment processes, so a lead who is hiring can focus on assessing the person rather than running the process


You

Most people who can do this job have around five years in games production behind them. Take that as a description of who tends to apply, not a bar we hold. If you can show us the things below with less, please apply anyway. We would rather meet you than miss you.

  • You know how games get made across disciplines: what waits on what, how long things really take, and where a plan is optimistic before the dates say so

  • You have produced across several titles and taken at least one PC title all the way to release, including the closing stretch: feature lock, bug burn, submission, the go decision. Which store matters less than that you have been through a PC launch. Projects that were cancelled along the way still count; we know how the last few years have gone for a lot of good people

  • You have owned priorities, not just a schedule. You have made cut-or-keep calls on a shipped title and lived with them, and you can tell us about one you got wrong

  • You have worked closely with a founder, studio head or creative director, and you know how to take decisions off their plate without going around them

  • You have built and driven a schedule, and you have written down a way of working that other people picked up and used. We would love to see examples, in whatever form they exist

  • You have led a team to a target without burning it out, and the people on it would work with you again

  • You are proactive by default and you work independently. You do not wait to be asked or chased; given an assignment, you find out what it needs and finish it well without someone checking each step. That is what senior means to us

  • Leads tell you how things are really going, because you talk with them directly and they trust you with the real picture

  • You are fluent in Jira at the level of owning it for a team, Jira Plans included. It is a tool, not the job, but it is the tool we run the plan through, so we need you good with it

  • You work our day, which runs on CET; where you sit while you do is up to you. And you are comfortable working in English, written and spoken


Helpful, not required

  • Steam specifically: Steamworks, builds and depots, the store page, review and submission, and how Early Access behaves through the whole run

  • Live operations and a patch cadence

  • Working with external production partners before, on either side of the relationship

  • Time at a small studio where you were the only producer, or where the producer and product owner were the same person

  • A remote-first team


What we offer

The whole project and the authority that comes with it. Real decisions, not just a schedule to report against. Strong leads beside you rather than under you, and a Creative Director who wants to hand things over and means it. A company small enough that what you do is visible in what we ship, and people who will notice.

We are a self-motivated team, remote by choice and flexible in how we work, and we run on people helping each other rather than watching each other. Everyone here is trusted to own their part and supported when they need a hand, and we would like that to be true for you from your first week.

And we are early. Scape is heading to Steam with everything still ahead of it. Joining now means building something with a real chance of becoming big, and being one of the people it belongs to when it does.


Practical

  • Remote. Our working day runs on CET and this role keeps it.

  • Full time, on a long-term contract.

  • Start: as soon as you can. Tell us your notice period in the application form and we will work around it.

  • Recruitment is ongoing.

Role Title: Growth Manager - Monetization
Team: Growth Systems

Who You Will Work With:

  • Manager: Julien Ceddaha, Growth Systems Lead

  • Direct Reports: None

  • Key Cross-Functional Collaborators: Product, Design, Engineering, CRM/Lifecycle, Data

Location: Remote. Paris hybrid welcome, but not required.


Why Opal?

  • Mission-Driven Impact: We are on a mission to help 1Bn people to focus better every day. We've empowered our community to save 500M+ hours and counting.

  • Ownership & Flexibility: Structure your work to foster creativity and productivity.

  • Collaborative Culture: Work with a small, high-impact team that gathers quarterly for meetups and learning. Nearly $1M in Revenue per Employee.

  • Growth & Recognition: Join a top-30 US productivity app with competitive compensation and early equity. 4.8/5 rating on 60k+ reviews, and past $15M in ARR.

  • Well-Supported: Backed by world-class investors and founders of companies like Pinterest, Snapchat, and Revolut.

Why This Role and Why Now?

At Opal, we're building tools to help people reclaim their time and focus on what truly matters. As we continue to grow and save millions of hours of screen time for our community, we’re looking for a Monetization Manager to accelerate growth and take ownership of B2C revenue generation.

Here's why this is the perfect moment to join:

  • Ownership & Impact: You'll take the lead on paywall and offer experimentation, pricing and packaging, Android and Web monetization, and lifecycle recovery. Working directly with Julien (Growth Systems Lead) and closely with Product, Design and Engineering.

  • Your Role in Growth Systems: You'll be the dedicated monetization owner on a small, high-ownership team, stepping into a fast-growing company where your work will directly shape the future of focus, productivity, and Opal's revenue engine. Within six months, you'll own the monetization roadmap end-to-end and be running several revenue initiatives in parallel.


What You'll Be Doing

As our Monetization Manager, you will:

  1. Own paywall and offer experimentation, end-to-end. This is where most of your week goes. You'll run the test pipeline on onboarding and in-app surfaces: pick the hypothesis, build the paywall yourself, ship it, read it on revenue per user, and call it win / kill / scale. We need someone who builds, not someone who briefs and waits.

  2. Own pricing. Shape the price ladder, plan architecture, trial design, intro offers and eligibility, discounting, and geo/PPP pricing bands - owning the model behind the price, not just the price itself.

  3. Grow Android and Web monetization. These are the two platforms with the clearest headroom versus iOS, and a direct unlock for future growth investment on those surfaces.

  4. Build monetization surfaces inside the product itself. Feature gating, entitlements, and contextual upsell in the context of the feature itself - partnering closely with Product, Design and Engineering to design and land these.

  5. Own recovery and lifecycle monetization. Trial-cancel win-back, abandoned transactions, churn recovery, and referral offers. You own the offer and its economics, CRM owns the channel.

What You Bring

  • 3 to 5 years owning monetization at a consumer subscription app. You can point to a paywall, a price, or an offer that shipped because of you.

  • You build it yourself. Hands-on experience implementing paywalls in a paywall tool (Superwall, RevenueCat, Adapty, or equivalent).

  • Self-serve on data and AI. Comfortable with self-served BI, product analytics, and subscription reporting; you can size an opportunity and read an experiment without an analyst holding your hand.

  • You own the pricing model. You've built a price ladder or elasticity view and can defend it with numbers.

  • You know the stores. Deep familiarity with App Store Connect and Play Console subscription mechanics - subscription groups, intro offers and eligibility, win-back offers, price changes, and store review constraints on paywalls.

  • Experimentation rigour. You write a hypothesis and a numeric prediction before you launch, respect guardrails and cohort maturity, and report losses as readily as wins.

  • English required. French preferred, not required.

Bonus points for:

  • Android monetization at scale, or experience with web2app or Stripe funnels.

  • Geo and PPP pricing run across several markets, including the localization and reporting nuances that come with it.

  • An AI-native way of working - we run much of this stack with agents.

  • Copy and design taste on paywalls, grounded in applied behavioural psychology.

  • Experience somewhere small enough that you had to close the whole loop yourself.

If you're ready to shape the future of focus and productivity, we'd love to meet you!

Compensation: €50K – €70K • €20K – €60K Equity

Rejoindre Sunrock, c'est intégrer une entreprise européenne en forte croissance, où autonomie, collaboration et impact vont de pair avec l'ambition d'accélérer la transition énergétique.

Missions principales

  • Droit des contrats et droit des affaires. Participation à la rédaction, à la revue et à la négociation des contrats liés aux projets photovoltaïques, notamment les contrats de bail emphytéotique, les baux civils, les conventions d'occupation du domaine public, les contrats EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction).

    Des connaissances en legal design et en process seraient un plus très apprécié. 

  • Veille juridique. Réalisation de recherches juridiques et de notes de synthèse sur des sujets d'actualité liés au secteur de l'énergie solaire et, plus largement, aux énergies renouvelables.

En 5 hashtags, ça donne 👉 #CRM #CustomerLifecycle #MarketingAutomation #CustomerIntelligence #NextBestAction

🍒 sur le 🎂 : tu arrives pile au moment où tout se construit, migration vers un nouvel outil d'orchestration multicanale, déploiement d'un outil de Next Best Action, budget de fonctionnement CRM en hausse de 40% et lancement d'un nouveau plan stratégique à 3 ans.

🚀 Tes missions principales :

  • Piloter le plan de communication client dans son ensemble : emails commerciaux, automatisés et transactionnels.

  • Définir la stratégie CRM et la roadmap Customer Lifecycle, pour sortir des triggers purement produits et capitaliser sur les moments de vie client.

  • Faire de la connaissance client un avantage compétitif : piloter les outils data, produire des insights actionnables et évangéliser la culture client en interne.

  • Construire le “Next Best Action” et l'orchestration augmentée par l'IA, pour passer d'un CRM intuitif à un CRM cognitif où la décision d'adressage, le canal, la pression et l'offre sont finement automatisés.

  • Piloter la performance client de bout en bout : indicateurs digitaux et business, ventes croisées, réactivation, revenu par client, repeat, lifetime value.

  • Manager et faire monter en compétences ton équipe de 4 collaboratrices (toutes les 4 sont des Pépites !).

  • Devenir le·la partenaire interne des équipes marketing, produit, data et tech.

💛 Ton équipe :

  • L'entreprise : un comparateur digital dans les secteurs de l’assurance et des services financiers, créé il y a 14 ans et réunissant une centaine de personnes à son siège parisien. En forte croissance, sa culture est tech, rapide et collaborative.

  • Ton équipe : 4 personnes aux métiers complémentaires : une PMO CRM, une responsable de la communication client, une cheffe de projet campagnes et une alternante en production. Une équipe compétente, motivée et franchement top !

  • Ton manager : le CMO, tout juste promu en interne après avoir lui-même porté le périmètre CRM. Très humain et motivant pour ses équipes, c’est un véritable manager-mentor : il connaît le sujet à fond, accompagne la progression de chacun·e et donne les moyens de réussir.

  • Tes interlocuteurs : tu évolues au sein d’une équipe marketing d’une trentaine de personnes, avec des expertises clés en SEO, acquisition payante, marque, contenu et service client. Tu collabores également avec les équipes data, produit et tech, ainsi qu’avec tes homologues à l’international.

💻 Tes Conditions de travail :

  • Ton bureau : de très beaux bureaux, hyper agréables, dans le 17ème arrondissement de Paris, à côté du Parc Monceau.

  • Le midi : pas de cantine, mais une carte tickets restaurant.

  • Ton package de rémunération :

    • Salaire 100% fixe : entre 65 et 80k€ brut annuels, selon expérience.

    • Participation/Intéressement : participation jusqu'à 10% du salaire annuel selon les objectifs d'entreprise (rentabilité, marge), soit jusqu’à 8k€/an. Un intéressement est en cours de mise en place.

    • Autres avantages : très bonne mutuelle, prime annuelle de vacances (environ 800€ cette année), primes culture et sport, soirées au minimum une fois par mois.

  • Ton rythme :

    • 5 semaines de congés payés

    • Une dizaine de jours de RTT par an.

    • Jusqu’à 3 jours de télétravail par semaine (et encore plus de souplesse sur juillet/août).

    • Possibilité de semaine en full-remote durant les fêtes de fin d’année.


Tes expériences & compétences :

  • Tu as piloté un périmètre CRM de bout en bout, avec la responsabilité du business et pas seulement de la stratégie ou de l'implémentation d'outils.

  • Tu maîtrises les outils du marché type Batch, Braze, Salesforce ou équivalents.

  • Tu as construit une stratégie CRM et une roadmap Customer Lifecycle, avec des parcours automatisés et transactionnels.

  • Tu connais les sujets “Next Best Action” et orchestration augmentée par l'IA.

  • Tu pilotes tes KPI digitaux et business : ventes croisées, réactivation, revenu par client, repeat, lifetime value.

  • Tu as déjà managé hiérarchiquement une équipe.

  • Tu parles anglais couramment, c'est indispensable pour travailler avec le groupe.

  • Une expérience du secteur de la banque/assurance ou en marketplace serait appréciée.

  • Avoir vécu une organisation BU et centrale serait un vrai plus pour comprendre la dynamique groupe.

  • Les profils “annonceur” comme “conseil” sont bienvenus, à condition d'avoir réellement piloté du business sur le terrain.

Ta personnalité :

  • Visionnaire et analytique, tu pars des chiffres et du contexte pour poser une vision client, et surtout tu sais la raconter.

  • Pédagogue et collaboratif·ve, tu embarques le marketing, la data, le produit et la tech, parce que la culture client s'évangélise autant qu'elle se pilote.

  • Manager bienveillant·e et exigeant·e, tu aimes faire grandir une équipe jeune, motivée et déjà très sachante.

  • À l'aise avec le changement, tu as envie de créer plutôt que de faire tourner l'existant.

Mon avis de recruteuse sur ce job :

C'est un poste pour quelqu'un qui aime construire : la maturité CRM est à 50%, la vision client à 20%, et les moyens sont là, budget en hausse et nouveaux outils en cours de déploiement. J'aime le fait que le manager ait tenu le périmètre avant toi, il sait exactement de quoi il parle et où il veut aller. Si tu cherches un CRM à faire passer du running à un vrai levier de croissance, dans une boîte tech et très peu politique, tu es au bon endroit.

Unison is a telecom and renewables infrastructure investment firm funded in partnership with Ardian - the global investment house based in Paris with over $150 billion in assets under management. Unison commenced operations in 2003 and today invests in real estate and infrastructure hosting wireless and renewables tenants in the United States and Europe. The Company is expanding rapidly and looking for talented, entrepreneurial team members to grow with us. 

JOB TITLE
 
Job Title (EN): Business Development / Origination Manager (France)
Job Title (FR): Responsable Développement Commercial / Origination (France)
 
 
LOCATION
 
Location (EN): France (Hybrid / Remote depending on region)
Localisation (FR): France (Hybride / Télétravail selon la région)
 
 
COMPENSATION
 
Compensation (EN): Competitive base salary + performance-based commission
Rémunération (FR): Rémunération fixe compétitive + commission liée à la performance
 
 
ABOUT THE ROLE | À PROPOS DU POSTE
 
EN:
We are looking for a commercially driven Business Development / Origination Manager to identify, structure, negotiate, and close real-estate and land-related transactions in France. You will manage the full deal lifecycle—from sourcing and first contact through negotiation to closing—while building and maintaining a healthy sales pipeline.

Nous recherchons un/une Responsable Développement Commercial / Origination à forte orientation commerciale pour identifier, structurer, négocier et conclure des transactions liées à l’immobilier et au foncier en France. Business Development Manager; Origination Manager; Commercial Manager; Land Acquisition Manager; Site Acquisition Manager; Real Estate Transactions Manager; Deal Originator; Sales Manager (Real Estate)

Responsable Développement Commercial; Business Developer; Responsable Commercial; Responsable Acquisition Foncière; Responsable Foncier; Responsable Transactions Immobilières; Real Estate Manager; Deal Manager

- Être le premier point de contact des prospects avec une approche de vente consultative

- Contribuer à l’amélioration des outils CRM, de la génération de leads et des processus d’origination
- Participer aux initiatives stratégiques et au développement du marché en France
 
 
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR | PROFIL RECHERCHÉ
 
Required | Requis
 
EN:
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in sales or business development
- Proven experience in negotiating and closing transactions end-to-end
- Strong business acumen and structured approach to pipeline management
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 
FR:
- Diplôme de niveau Bac+3 minimum ou expérience professionnelle équivalente en vente ou développement commercial
- Expérience avérée en négociation et en conclusion de transactions (end-to-end)
- Solide compréhension business et approche structurée de la gestion de pipeline
- Excellentes compétences en communication et relations interpersonnelles
 
 
Nice to Have | Atouts

- Familiarity with real estate closing processes

FR:
- Connaissance des processus de closing en immobilier

- Expérience dans l’immobilier, les télécoms, les énergies renouvelables, les infrastructures ou la finance
 
 
PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES | QUALITÉS PERSONNELLES

Entrepreneurial mindset, high integrity, strong negotiation skills, results-oriented, and comfortable working in a dynamic environment.
 
FR:
Esprit entrepreneurial, haut niveau d’intégrité, fortes compétences en négociation, orientation résultats et aisance dans un environnement dynamique.
 
 
WHAT WE OFFER | CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

Competitive compensation structure including base salary and performance-based commission, high level of autonomy, and professional growth opportunities.

Un package de rémunération attractif comprenant un fixe et une commission liée à la performance, un haut niveau d’autonomie et des opportunités d’évolution professionnelle.

développement commercial, origination, acquisition foncière, foncier, transactions immobilières, négociation, closing, gestion de pipeline, CRM, génération de leads

Biggie est un groupe de conseil en communication, né de la fusion de l’agence média Repeat, du trading desk Gamned!, du studio de création vidéo Kazam et de l’agence en stratégie d’influence Beastly.
 
Comprenant 300 collaborateurs et des filiales dans de nombreux pays (France, Belgique, Suisse, Italie, République Tchèque, Emirats Arabes Unis, Brésil…), le groupe s’appuie sur sa capacité à fédérer l’excellence, via l’intégration d’expertises publicitaires leader de leur marché, de manière à concevoir et piloter des stratégies de communication 360 à l'échelle l’internationale.

En tant que Responsable Comptable Général, vous êtes garant(e) de l’ensemble des opérations comptables et financières. Vous supervisez la production des états financiers dans le respect des normes comptables en vigueur et assurez la qualité et la fiabilité des informations financières à destination des parties prenantes internes et externes.
 
Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec tous les services de la Finance (Comptabilité Clients, Comptabilité Fournisseurs, l’ADV et le contrôle de gestion), le service des ressources humaines et le service juridique et serez garant de la fluidité des échanges.
 
🗒️ Missions
 
1- Gestion quotidienne de la tenue de la comptabilité et le bon suivi des obligations comptables et fiscales : 
• Garantir la bonne tenue des écritures comptables dans le respect des normes françaises (et éventuellement internationales type IFRS si applicable).
• Echange continu et régulier avec la comptabilité fournisseurs et la comptabilité clients
• Assurer le bon suivi de l’établissement des déclarations fiscales (TVA, IS, CVAE, CFE, DAS2, etc.)
• Être le(la) référent(e) en matière de veille fiscale et garantir la conformité des pratiques aux obligations légales en vigueur.
 
2- Etablissement des clôtures périodiques (mensuelle, trimestrielle, annuelle) et Audit des comptes: 
• Etablir les clôtures complètes, analyse détaillée et formalisation des comptes et des
provisions
• Préparer les reportings périodiques financiers et comptables destinés à la Direction Financière et à la Direction Générale
• Etablir les états financiers et les annexes aux comptes annuels
• Assurer l’audit des comptes en étant le point de contact principal.
 
3- Management d’équipe : 
• Encadrer et animer une équipe comptable (recrutement, formation, montée en compétences des collaborateurs)
• Veiller à l'organisation et à la répartition des tâches au sein de l'équipe au quotidien et en période de clôture pour garantir le respect des deadlines
 
4- Projets transverses :
• Participer à la mise en place et/ou à l’amélioration des outils comptables et des processus internes
• Accompagner les projets de transformation liés à la digitalisation des fonctions financières
 
👉 Profil recherché
 
Formation et expérience :
• Issu(e) d’une formation supérieure en comptabilité, gestion ou finance (DSCG, Master CCA, École de Commerce ou équivalent)
• Expérience confirmée (5 à 8 ans minimum) en comptabilité générale, idéalement dans un environnement multi-sites/multi-sociétés ou en cabinet d'expertise comptable/audit avant un poste en entreprise
• Une expérience dans le secteur des médias ou une familiarité avec les spécificités liées au secteur serait un plus
 
Compétences techniques :
• Maîtrise des normes comptables françaises et idéalement IFRS
• Excellente connaissance des logiciels comptables et ERP (exemples : SAP, Sage, Oracle, etc.)
• Maîtrise avancée d’Excel
• Bonne compréhension des outils de dématérialisation et des processus de digitalisation comptable
• Bon niveau dans la pratique de l’anglais (écrit et oral)
 
Qualités personnelles :
• Rigoureux(se), Organisé(e), Structuré(e) et Polyvalent(e)
• Leader d’équipe ayant d’excellentes capacités managériales
• Sens de la communication et capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs variés
• Sensibilité aux délais et esprit de priorisation.
 
Informations pratiques
  • 📅 Contrat : CDI 
  • 💰 Rémunération : entre 55K et 65K en package (fixe + variable)
  • 📍 Lieu : Paris

• Des entités pluridisciplinaires expertes dans leur domaine : programmatique, influence, RP, 360, création de contenus… 
• Possibilité de mobilité interne au sein des différentes entités du groupe

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

Studio has been developed to help enterprises build, evaluate, and operate AI systems reliably, safely, and at scale, turning prototypes into production-ready solutions. It provides the infrastructure enterprises need to scale their use cases, including comprehensive monitoring, reliable automation, and centralized tracking of AI assets.

We are seeking a strong product leader to own the strategy and shape the future of Studio redefining the AI builder experience in enterprises.

You will determine how enterprises observe AI behavior, run complex workflows, version and track assets, and deploy safely across hybrid and self-hosted environments.

What You Will do

  • Strategy & Vision - Define and evangelize the product vision, strategy and annual goals for Studio. You will be accountable for its business impact.

  • Team leadership - Build the Studio PM organization: hire PMs and stream leads, set the operating cadence (quarterly product reviews, roadmap reviews…), and develop PMs through clear growth paths.

  • Delivery & Execution - Partner with engineering leadership on the roadmap to scope, sequence, and deliver value by balancing quick wins for our customers while advancing the long-term platform bets.

  • Drive strategic customer discovery with the PMs under your responsibility.

  • Go-to-market - Collaborate with Marketing and Go-to-market teams on positioning, pricing and packaging, launch plans, and adoption strategies.

  • Partner cross-functionally and with other product leaders to ensure we have a unified customer journey.

What We're Looking For

  • 10+ years in product management, with deep experience building technical platform, infrastructure or developer products for enterprise customers and AI/ML fluency

  • Proven people leadership: you've hired and grown senior PMs, organized teams around clear stream ownership, and built durable operating cadences

  • Experience launching and scaling products

  • Proven ability to align and inspire cross-functional teams without direct authority.

  • Ownership and pragmatism: low ego, high EQ, bias for action; equally comfortable crafting a strategy narrative and diving into metrics, UX details, or a customer escalation

  • Strong communication skills for executives, teams, and users.

  • Ability to thrive in dynamic environments where priorities shift.

  • Self-directed, taking initiative to navigate unknowns and own outcomes.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

Mistral AI partners with the leaders of their industries to redefine how their most complex, high-stakes challenges are solved with frontier AI.

As a Solutions Operations Manager for our strategic accounts, you act as the chief of staff to the account leadership: you sit at the heart of the transformation, working with the client's leadership and with Mistral's best deployment strategists, forward-deployed engineers and applied scientists. You keep every account running like clockwork and run point on operations to maximize the impact of Mistral's resources.

This is a hands-on role for someone who blends consulting-grade strategic thinking with the pragmatism of an operator, who embeds in their accounts and owns the outcome, and who brings AI into the day-to-day of the account.

What you'll do

As the operational backbone of the account, you will act as the Chief of Staff to the Program Lead, to ensure Mistral sets the high standard for execution, speed, and collaboration with the client. Your role blends strategic governance, hands-on project management, operational innovation, and internal automation to keep initiatives on track and stakeholders aligned.

Governance & Strategic Alignment

  • Ensure the Program Lead’s vision is clearly articulated and adopted by both Mistral’s account team and the client

  • Drive alignment between client stakeholders and Mistral teams to ensure shared priorities and high-quality delivery standards

  • Facilitate data-driven decision-making for leadership through weekly cadences, steering committee prep, and risk dashboards.

Strategic Scoping & Value Definition

  • Develop a deep understanding of the client’s business, operating model, and strategic priorities

  • Partner with the Program Lead and Account team to scope transformative programs, identify and define use cases, and build a clear business case and value framework

  • Translate strategic ambition into measurable outcomes and track the long-term business impact of each program

Delivery & Execution

  • Own delivery frameworks: timelines, milestones, reporting, proactively securing commitments and flagging risks or delays early.

  • Optimize delivery processes by identifying friction points and standardizing workflows to enhance quality and predictability.

Operational Innovation & Automation

  • Build and enhance Mistral’s platform and internal tools to empower program delivery with scalable, tailored solutions

  • Automate workflows to eliminate manual friction in planning, reporting, and follow-ups, accelerating execution and reducing operational overhead


Who you are

  • Strategic operator. You bring 3–5 years of experience in top-tier strategy consulting or as a Chief of Staff in top startup/scale-up, with the structured thinking, adaptability, and clear communication that comes with it.

  • AI-fluent. You genuinely use AI tools to automate your own work: drafting, analysis, reporting, PMO tasks. You're comfortable building and iterating on automations, not just prompting a chatbot.

  • High agency. You don't wait to be told what to do. You see the gap, you close it, and you raise the standard as you go.

  • Customer-centric. You can hold a room with senior enterprise stakeholders and translate between business strategy and technical delivery.

  • Meticulous and reliable. Ownership to the last detail; nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.

  • Adaptable. Comfortable operating in ambiguity and a fast-moving environment; bias to action over process for its own sake.


Nice to have

  • Experience in enterprise software, AI, or deep-tech delivery environments.

  • Exposure to change management / adoption at scale within large organizations.

  • Hands-on experience automating workflows with LLMs or building internal tooling.


Practical details

  • Location: Paris, with travel expected ~30% of your time to customer sites (Europe)

  • Team: Solutions Org, reporting into the Solutions leadership.

  • Scope: One or several strategic accounts.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As our VP of Global Developer Relations, you’ll be the voice and facilitator of Mistral to the developer, scientific, and technical communities. You’ll build and scale a global DevRel strategy that fosters deep engagement, advocacy, and love for Mistral’s models and technology. Your team will build communities and educate, excite, and empower developers to adopt, innovate, and evangelize Mistral’s technology—whether they’re startups, enterprises, researchers, or open-source contributors.

You’ll work closely with Product, Research, Engineering, Marketing, Communications, and more to ensure developers have the tools, resources, and inspiration they need to succeed with Mistral.

What You Will Do

Build a Global Developer Movement

  • Develop and execute a global DevRel strategy that connects Mistral and our AI platform effectively with developers, scientists, and technologists.

  • Create authentic, developer-first engagement—focusing on education, inspiration, and community, with great content and AI tools.

  • Foster a culture of advocacy where developers naturally champion Mistral in their networks, projects, and conversations.

Engage and Inspire the Technical Community

  • Lead high-impact developer engagement initiatives, including:

    • Technical content (e.g., tutorials, blog posts, videos, documentation) that helps developers get started, optimize, and innovate with Mistral’s models.

    • Community programs (e.g., hackathons, meetups, AMAs, Discord/Slack communities) that bring together AI builders, researchers, and enthusiasts.

    • Evangelism & thought leadership (e.g., conference talks, podcasts, technical deep dives) that showcase Mistral’s unique value and capabilities.

  • Work with Product and Research teams to translate complex AI innovations into accessible, exciting, and actionable insights for developers.

Enable Developer Success, particularly for self-service adoption

  • Build scalable enablement programs (e.g., onboarding guides, SDKs, APIs, sample projects) that reduce friction for developers adopting Mistral’s models.

  • Create feedback loops between the developer community and Mistral’s Product/Engineering teams to shape the roadmap based on real-world needs.

Scale a World-Class DevRel Team

  • Hire, mentor, and lead a global team of Developer Advocates, Engineers and Evangelists - with particular strength in Europe and San Francisco

  • Define metrics and KPIs to measure the impact of DevRel (e.g., developer adoption, community growth, engagement, advocacy).

  • Lead from the front as a fantastic representative of Mistral at events, in social, and in project communities

Drive Open Source & Ecosystem Growth

  • Champion open-source contributions and collaborative innovation around Mistral’s models.

  • Partner with startups, enterprises, and academic institutions to accelerate adoption and co-innovation.

  • Identify and nurture key developer influencers, maintainers, and ambassadors who can amplify Mistral’s reach and impact.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven leadership in Developer Relations, Developer Marketing, or Technical Evangelism for a B2B technology company, preferably in AI, cloud, and open-source.

  • Deep technical credibility—ability to engage with developers, scientists, and engineers on their terms (e.g., code, research, architecture).

  • Passion for community building—a track record of growing and nurturing technical communities (e.g., open-source projects, developer forums, hackathons).

  • Strong storytelling and communication skills—ability to simplify complex concepts and inspire developers through content, talks, and interactions.

  • Strategic and operational excellence—ability to scale DevRel globally while maintaining a hands-on, authentic approach.

  • Collaborative mindset—ability to work across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales to align DevRel with Mistral’s broader goals.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Experience in AI, machine learning, or large language models (LLMs).

  • Personally contributed meaningfully to open source projects and communities.

  • Led global DevRel teams in high-growth, competitive markets.

  • Personal brand or following in the developer or AI community Experience launching and scaling developer-focused products or tools.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

 L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous :

En tant que postdoctorant, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au au Centre Microélectronique de Provence, département Bioélectronique. Au sein de ce service vous vous contribuez à une recherche interdisciplinaire au service de l’innovation scientifique et sociétale.

Entité :

Le Département Bioélectronique du Centre Microélectronique de Provence développe des technologies innovantes à l’interface entre électronique, matériaux et sciences du vivant. Implanté à Gardanne, au cœur de la région Aix-Marseille, il dispose d’un environnement de recherche de pointe et d’une salle blanche entièrement équipée.
Ses équipes évoluent dans un contexte international et interdisciplinaire, en collaboration étroite avec des partenaires académiques et cliniques.

Objectif stratégique du recrutement :

Renforcer les capacités de recherche du Département Bioélectronique avec un postdoctorant capable de développer une nouvelle génération de capteurs optiques organiques flexibles pour l’imagerie calcique in vivo.
Ce recrutement contribuera à faire progresser une technologie à fort potentiel à l’interface entre microélectronique, bioélectronique et neurosciences.

Missions principales :

·         Vous développez et micro-fabriquez des photodétecteurs organiques flexibles sous forme de matrices multipixels haute résolution.

·         Vous développez le système d’acquisition permettant la lecture parallèle des différents pixels.

·         Vous assurez le conditionnement, la caractérisation et le benchmarking physico-optique du capteur en environnement biologique.

·         Vous analysez et évaluez les performances du capteur dans le cadre d’expérimentations in vivo, en collaboration avec l’Institut de Neurosciences de la Timone (INT).

·         Vous valorisez vos travaux par des publications scientifiques et des communications internationales.

Votre capacité à travailler de manière autonome dans un environnement interdisciplinaire et à faire le lien entre recherche fondamentale, développement technologique et applications en santé sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons :

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

·         Diplôme de niveau Bac + 5 ou équivalent

·         Titulaire d’un doctorat (ou êtes sur le point de l’obtenir), de préférence en génie électrique, microélectronique, génie biomédical, physique, chimie, science des matériaux ou génie chimique.

Et idéalement :

·      Titulaire d’un diplôme de doctorat

·      Avec une expérience de 3 ans dans l’électronique organique

·      Junior accepté : oui

·      Une expérience significative en microfabrication et travail en salle blanche

·      Une expérience confirmée en électronique organique et/ou en fabrication de photodétecteurs

·      Une expertise avérée en caractérisation électrique et optique

·      Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1) et de Matlab ou Python pour l’analyse de données

 

Vos atouts supplémentaires :

·         Une expérience en électronique organique et/ou dans le domaine des cellules solaires

·         Une expérience en caractérisation de capteurs ou de dispositifs optoélectroniques

·         Un intérêt marqué pour les recherches interdisciplinaires à l’interface entre électronique, matériaux et sciences du vivant

·         Une expérience dans un environnement de recherche international serait appréciée

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver :

·           Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain

·           Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

·           Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens.
